chunks: Narrated to us my father, may God be pleased with him, who said: Sa'd ibn Abdullah narrated to us, who said: Ahmad ibn Abi Abdullah al-Barqi, through his chain, raised it to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him)
Regarding the saying of God, the Exalted: 'Did We not give you long enough life so that he that would should receive admonition?' He said: 'A rebuke for one who is eighteen years old.'
ai.seo_question: What is the age of accountability according to Imam al-Sadiq in this verse?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Al-Khisal*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) interprets the phrase 'long enough life' in Surah Ar-Ra'd as a specific benchmark for the onset of intellectual maturity and accountability, setting the minimum age at eighteen years. This interpretation highlights the Shia scholarly emphasis on the development of reason (*'aql*) as the primary criterion for *taklif*, distinguishing it from mere chronological age. The hadith serves as a foundational reference for understanding the threshold of moral responsibility in Islamic jurisprudence.
